freeze_semantics: Content-hash freeze of the vibe adapter's output over the conformance scenarios at harness 2.4.x (archived anchor). vibe uses the preprocess path: preprocess_vibe.py normalises native session DIRECTORIES (meta.json + messages.jsonl each) into a container array, which vibe.dsl.yaml turns into one trace per session — vibe is the fleet's only multi-trace adapter (sessions: DSL), so dsl_runner itself resolves cross-trace lineage placeholders and stamps content_hash (verify.py asserts the stamp and must NOT re-run back-fill, per cross_trace R2). verify.py re-runs preprocess+DSL on each input (cwd = this dir, input paths relative) and asserts trace_count, per-trace content_hash, and unmapped_path_count. vibe traces carry no provenance.source_path, so the content_hash is checkout-independent. The container-batch scenario (5 sessions, one batch) exercises the multi-trace emission path; s3-modify (a single session dir) exercises the single-session input shape — its hash equals trace 3 of the batch, confirming batch-context independence for lineage-free sessions.
capture_provenance: Archived container capture (2026-03-16T03:56-03:57Z, the 2026-03-16-container-run batch): mistral-vibe in the March scenario-runner container (python:3.12-slim, /workspace, devstral-2 via api.mistral.ai behind a capture proxy), scenarios S1-S5 of the shared scenario set. VERSION IS DATE-BOUND, NOT IN-BAND: vibe carries no version identifier anywhere in its session output (meta.json has no version field), and the runner Dockerfile pinning mistral-vibe==2.4.2 was committed 2026-03-31 — AFTER this capture — so it corroborates but cannot prove the exact patch level. What the dates DO prove: the capture finished at 2026-03-16T03:57Z, before 2.5.0's PyPI release the same day at 16:54Z, and 2.4.0/2.4.1/2.4.2 released 03-09/03-10/03-12 — so the binary was 2.4.x (latest available: 2.4.2). Format era confirmed 2.4-era in-band (no title_source / parent_session_id / loops in meta.json). Hence the rung label 2.4.x, not a point version.
